content.content:
Hi all,



For Monday, so we're talking about the same thing. The store builds players have today are iOS 0.3.49 (Leonard released it yesterday) and Android 0.3.133. Both were cut from main on Sep 26, and everything difficulty related was merged long before that.



The level editor (Assets/Scripts/LevelEditor and the LevelDesigner panels), anything in an Editor folder and the debug menu (Assets/Scripts/Debug) are stripped from store builds. A ticket whose changes are only level editor or debug tooling never reached players, Done or not.



Blake

On tier -2 one win promotes you.\\nDemotion: 4 losses in a row moves you down one tier.\\n\\nBlunder: overfilling the match bar enrages every monster on the board: +25% walk speed, +25% damage, +25% max HP (ZOM-254, values per monster).\"}"}

{"id": "ZOM-42", "uuid": null, "identifier": "ZOM-42", "number": 42, "title": "Dynamic Difficulty", "description": "# **Part 1:**

Allow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)

What's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.

* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)
* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)

What's not identical in the tiers:

* Quantity of the items
* Quantity of the monsters
* Pre-warm period

Players starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.

Demotion Rules based on win streak:

1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)
2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.

Promotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.
2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player
3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this "early exit" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.

Demotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.
2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.

Please note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.

This also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.

A losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.

# **Part 2: Future expansion**

If a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:

Monster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with

Punk A | Punk B

Punk B | Punk C

Punk C | Punk D

Punk D | Brute A

Boss 1 | Boss 3

Boss 2 | Boss 4

Boss 10 | Boss 10

If the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.

The other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster "rank" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the "next rank" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:
Punk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C

values: How it works in the store builds today (iOS 0.3.49 / Android 0.3.133)

Each level has tier versions -2 to +2; tier 0 is the default version (ZOM-42). Player tier is clamped to -2..+5 in code; the level loads the version for the player's tier, or the closest one the level has.
ZOM-42; Robert's 'how tiers work' deck; TierManager.cs on main

Set once, after the first 10 levels: average CPM over those 10 above 90 starts you on tier 1, everyone else stays on tier 0. The check is cpm > 90, so exactly 90 stays on tier 0. (ZOM-199 and Robert's deck say 90 or more; the build never changed from the original spec.)
Blake's reply to 'store builds for monday' (Sep 30); ZOM-42

Tier -2: one win promotes you one tier. Tier -1 and up: win rate of 80% or more over the last (up to) 10 attempts promotes you one tier, with early exit (e.g. 8 wins in a row is enough). The attempt record resets after every promotion or demotion.

Tier -1 and up: 4 losses in a row demotes you one tier, at any time. Also, a win rate of 50% or lower over the last (up to) 10 attempts demotes you one tier, with early exit (e.g. LLWLLL). Tier -2 is never demoted. The attempt record resets after every promotion or demotion. (Robert's deck lists only the 4-loss rule; ZOM-42 has both.)
Yes. When you are demoted, the level you were on reloads one tier version lower than it normally would, and stays lowered until you win it. After that the next level loads normally for your tier.

Blunder (overfilling the match bar) enrages every monster on the board instead of the old HP penalty. Enrage adds speed and damage only; the HP boost was switched off on Jun 19. Values are per monster (below).

• Live: 22
• Editor only: 9
• Replaced: 1 (ZOM-254, replaced by ZOM-282)

On the rules tab, Mailman, Mayor2 and PartyGirl show enrage as "not copied yet", because that's how the Live tab has them.

content.text:
I built the register following the rules on Leonard's "Difficulty baseline (Julia)" Trello card, put it in the ZM Difficulty folder, added the two ticket comments his rules call for, and replied to him in the DM.

**The register:** [ZM difficulty baseline register](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1CkB-LtAkAciuB9P4ZhBaQ9PwYBZawF_PnzhvSKv_-QY/edit) has two tabs, Tickets and Rules in force, as the session agenda asks. It's shared with everyone on Monday's tuning invite: Robert can edit; Leonard, Blake and Brian can comment.

**Tickets: 35 made the list.**

| Status | Count | Tickets |
|---|---|---|
| Live | 22 | |
| Editor only | 9 | |
| Replaced | 1 | ZOM-254, replaced by ZOM-282 |
| Not shipped | 3 | ZOM-202, ZOM-280, ZOM-293 |

- 31 tickets match on title words; Leonard's card comment added "attack power" to that word list. Blake's closing notes that start with "tiers:" add four more: ZOM-221, 300, 305 and 378.
- I left out the two duplicates, ZOM-203 and ZOM-276.
- Status is judged against Blake's store builds mail: tools that are stripped from store builds count as "Editor only."

**Judgement calls you might be asked about on Monday:**
- **ZOM-312 is Editor only.** Its code change touches shared game files, but Blake's closing note says those changes are only used by the level editor.
- **ZOM-45 is Live.** It sounds like editor work, but Blake's note says the game reads the difficulty label when it loads a level.

**Rules in force tab:**
- I checked each rule against the game code. That code was last changed Sep 20, before the Sep 26 store builds were cut.
- **Robert's deck is out of date in three places:**
  - Starting tier: it says 90 or more, but the build checks above 90, so exactly 90 stays on tier 0.
  - Demotion: it lists only the 4-losses-in-a-row rule. The build also demotes when the win rate over the last 10 attempts is 50% or lower.
  - Enrage: it still shows a +25% HP boost, which was switched off on Jun 19.
- After a demotion, the level being played does drop one tier until the player wins it.
- The enrage table is copied exactly from the Live tab of your monster enrage sheet. Mailman, Mayor2 and PartyGirl show "not copied yet" because that's how the Live tab has them.

**Ticket comments:** I added one on ZOM-199, saying the build checks above 90 rather than 90 or more. I added one on ZOM-254, naming ZOM-282 as its replacement. No other tickets were touched.

**Slack:** Leonard's DM has the link, the 35 total and the count for each status.
